languages.name: Python
languages.first: Write a Celsius-to-Kelvin function. Test 0 °C → 273.15 K, reject values below absolute zero, and explain the difference between text input and numeric data.

languages.name: C++
languages.first: Compile a program that stores three component masses in std::vector<double> and prints their sum. Change one value, predict the output, then use the debugger to inspect the loop.

languages.name: MATLAB
languages.first: Create a vector of times and plot a simple linear temperature rise. Label time in seconds and temperature in degrees Celsius. Change the slope and explain what the units must be.

languages.name: C
languages.first: Write a function that accepts an unsigned status byte and reports whether bit 0 is set. Test the values 0, 1, 2, and 3, and explain each result in binary.

languages.name: Bash / Linux
languages.first: In a practice folder, run pwd and ls, then display the first five lines of a sample log with head. Explain what each command does before using a pipeline.

rover.name: Autonomous rovers
rover.title: A rover that knows when to ask for help.
rover.description: A camera spots a possible obstacle. A confidence check decides the image is ambiguous. The rover stops and records the evidence. Useful autonomy includes knowing when the information is not good enough.
parts: Python explores images and analyzes test runs.
C++ organizes robot components and messages.
MATLAB models motion and feedback.
C decodes a small sensor’s status.
Bash reruns the same experiment.

space.name: Space robotics
space.title: A robotic technician for hard-to-reach equipment.
space.description: A mechanism exchanges a mock thermal-control module, checks that it is seated, and reports a failed verification. This connects your servicing-robot interests to software with clear states, evidence, and recovery behavior.
parts: Python compares inspection images and logs.
C++ coordinates the task’s states and interfaces.
MATLAB explores mechanism and actuator dynamics.
C handles a simple instrument interface.
Bash preserves commands, configurations, and reports.

propulsion.name: Propulsion & flight
propulsion.title: Understand a result before trusting a simulation.
propulsion.description: Compare a simple published performance model against reference data, vary one assumption, and plot the difference. Early work can use supplied datasets; deeper propulsion analysis waits for thermodynamics, fluids, and chemistry.
parts: Python automates parameter studies and plots.
C++ helps extend simulation software later.
MATLAB supports numerical models and dynamics.
C provides embedded-data foundations when needed.
Bash makes batches of analysis repeatable.

habitat.name: Space habitats
habitat.title: Keep the equipment healthy, not just running.
habitat.description: A temperature trend changes after a fan slows. A model predicts the response; the measurements reveal the model’s limits. A benchtop dataset can introduce the same reasoning used in much more demanding thermal systems.
parts: Python detects trends and missing samples.
C++ structures a monitoring application.
MATLAB models the thermal response.
C interprets sensor flags and readings.
Bash runs a consistent daily analysis.
